solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Another setter was in first place? That's not clear

parts.note: Mudd is the FT pseudonym of a fellow crossword compiler, a nod to a colleague of Cincinnus
someone in first place led the field

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which compiler won, followed by an admission of confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: MUDD is the name another setter uses in the FT; the clue relies on solvers knowing FT setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something muddled is confused and lacking clarity, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Expressions of displeasure, say, in writing

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the abbreviation for a manuscript

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Ways of showing annoyance, for example on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbled complaints under one's breath are low noises showing discontent, a plural noun sense.

clue.text: Number for Chevalier that is Country or Jazz

parts.note: dix is French for ten, a number the French singer Maurice Chevalier would use
i.e. abbreviates id est, meaning that is
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A musical piece for Maurice Chevalier, described as either country music or jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country or Jazz' looks like two music genres; Country is wordplay and only Jazz defines.
explanation.definitionFit: This traditional New Orleans style is a form of early jazz music.

clue.text: Miss Tandy's last to see film director

parts.note: to miss something is to lose it

indicators.note: only the final letter of the actress's surname is taken

explanation.surface: Actress Jessica Tandy's final scene was due to be seen by a film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a title for Jessica Tandy, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Losey was an American director of British films such as The Servant.

clue.text: Perform sad song outside Stag's Head with penniless chap

indicators.note: the mournful song goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a dirge is a mournful song

indicators.note: only the leading letter of the word is taken
the chap loses P, the abbreviation for penny

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: Someone sings a mournful number around a stag party's leader and a broke companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perform' is the definition, not an instruction to sing; 'Stag's Head' suggests a pub name but gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a duty is to carry it out or perform it.

clue.text: Rider, heading off, left initially for trailer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken
the first letter of the surname is removed

parts.note: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines

explanation.surface: A horseman losing his head, with someone on the left, describing a straggler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is not a horseman but the novelist Rider Haggard, whose surname loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard trails behind the others, so one who lags is a trailer.

clue.text: Colour of honey, mostly, on slice of toast

indicators.note: the term of endearment loses its final letter

parts.note: honey and love are both terms of endearment
read as 'a slice of toast': A plus the first letter of toast

explanation.surface: Describing the shade of honey spread on a piece of toast.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue lacks 'a': only 'on a slice of toast' gives A plus T. The setter dropped the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovat is a muted greyish-green shade used in tweeds, so it names a colour.

clue.text: Killer fish and swine

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a rotter is a contemptible person, a swine

explanation.surface: A murderer described as a cold fish and a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotter kills by strangling with a cord or wire.

clue.text: Give everyone books

parts.note: all means everyone
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand everyone some reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to give out or assign a share.

clue.text: Time to find leads in North American race track

parts.note: a day is a period of time

indicators.note: the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A suggestion that it is the moment to find the front-runners in an American motor race.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytona International Speedway in Florida is a famous motor-racing circuit.

clue.text: Josh has not finished carrying cross in this state

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the cross inside it
the verb loses its last letter

parts.note: to josh is to tease
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: Someone called Josh, still not done, carrying a crucifix through a US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh' looks like a name but is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is one of the United States, so it fits 'this state'.

clue.text: Sarah has always entered separately

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Sally is a familiar form of the name Sarah
ever means always

explanation.surface: Sarah has always come in on her own.
explanation.definitionFit: Severally is a formal adverb meaning individually or one by one.

clue.text: So pale, sent back to front? Totally!

indicators.note: the final letter is moved from the back to the start

parts.note: very white means so pale

explanation.surface: Someone so pale they look reversed, completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back to front' moves the E of VERY WHITE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Every whit means in every respect, entirely.

clue.text: Cap for garden party?

parts.note: a garden is out of doors, and Chambers gives out as that which is outside
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A hat to wear at an outdoor party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark asks for OUT DO read as a do held outside, i.e. a garden party.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to better or surpass it.

clue.text: Hurt all there

definitions.meaning: being all there means being mentally sharp, clever

explanation.definitionFit: Smart means both to sting painfully and to be quick-witted.

clue.text: USA sure to order collection for union

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Arranging for America to sort out wedding preparations.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers before her marriage.

clue.text: Song recalled with Roundhead doffing cap in romantic setting

indicators.note: the reversed song holds the trimmed Roundhead within it
the song is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a song

indicators.note: the Roundhead loses his first letter

parts.note: Roundheads were Puritan supporters of Parliament in the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A tune remembered alongside a Parliamentarian soldier taking off his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were the Parliamentary side in England's seventeenth-century Civil War, many of them Puritans; 'romantic setting' points to Anthony Hope's fictional kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom of Anthony Hope's romances, a byword for romantic settings.

clue.text: Lord recruited for fitting car part

indicators.note: the nobleman is taken into the other word

parts.note: right means fitting or proper
an earl is a lord

explanation.surface: A nobleman enlisted for a fitting of some vehicle component.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamp at the back of a car is one of its parts.

clue.text: Playwright, slim one, in play

indicators.note: the letters are played about with, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dramatist, a thin one, appearing in a stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Simon was an American dramatist who wrote The Odd Couple.

clue.text: Man adored rock stars

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A man worshipped rock music celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock stars' reads as one phrase; 'rock' is the anagram signal and 'stars' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: The greatest bed for a hare is wing-shaped

parts.note: boxer Muhammad Ali called himself the greatest
a form is the hollow where a hare lies

explanation.surface: Claim that the finest resting place for a hare is shaped like a wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliform means shaped like a wing, from Latin ala.

clue.text: Regretful, I step outside

indicators.note: the step goes around the letter I

parts.note: a rung is a step on a ladder

explanation.surface: Someone sorry they went outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing means feeling regret over something, used here as an adjective.

clue.text: More righteous boatman with no separate deduction?

indicators.note: the two letters are taken away from separate places

parts.note: a gondolier is a Venetian boatman
taken as written, its letters removed one at a time

explanation.surface: A boatman questioning whether he can claim a separate tax deduction.
explanation.walkthrough: N and O come out of GONDOLIER from different places, not side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Godlier means more pious, more devout.

clue.text: Solid ground for graven images

indicators.note: ground up, the letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: Firm earth as a base for carved statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Idols are carved images worshipped as gods, the graven images of the Bible.

clue.text: Prime bits of offal put twinkle in cat's eye

indicators.note: the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Choice pieces of offal make a cat's eyes twinkle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat's eye' looks like a road stud, but 'cat's' gives only its first letter and 'eye' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is a jocular or technical word for the eye.

clue.text: Old places unfortunately laid low

indicators.note: things gone wrong suggest letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Ancient sites sadly flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something collapsed has fallen down, been laid low.

clue.text: Man with stony face?

definitions.meaning: a man's first name, as in the singer ... Richard

explanation.definitionFit: Cliff is both a male given name and a steep rock face.

clue.text: Motorists' group keeps gear for dog

indicators.note: the motoring organisation holds the gear inside it

parts.note: the AA is Britain's Automobile Association
kit is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: A motoring association looks after equipment for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Akita is a large Japanese breed of dog.

clue.text: Flying knight in Heart of Midlothian using a chopper

indicators.note: the knight goes inside the extracted letters
the central pair of letters of the place name is taken

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
hewing is cutting with an axe

explanation.surface: A knight in the Scottish county or Scott novel wielding an axe.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian is a Walter Scott novel and an Edinburgh football club, but here the centre of 'Midlothian' gives OT.
explanation.definitionFit: On the wing means in flight, flying.

clue.text: A doctor piercing two feet

indicators.note: the pieces go into the Roman numeral

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medic stabbing a pair of feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi are metrical feet of a short syllable then a long one.

clue.text: One told to lay on computer not able to hack it?

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
duff means useless, no good

explanation.surface: Someone instructed to install a computer that cannot cope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay on, Macduff' is Macbeth's challenge in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth says lay on to Macduff, so he is the one so told.

clue.text: As a teacher one may put one's foot in it

definitions.text: one may put one's foot in it
definitions.meaning: a sports shoe, which a foot goes into

explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is both a coach and a sports shoe.
